lastText: OGSHARP RAPORUHome19141915191619171918HARD MODE — EROSION 1/430 October 1918The Armistice on LemnosThe armistice is signed in the harbour of Mudros on 30 October, aboard a British battleship, by the delegation of an empire whose armies have been beaten on every front it has fought on. The Straits are open to the Allies, the army is to go home and the garrisons in Arabia, Syria and Mesopotamia are to surrender. The war that the empire entered at the order of one minister and one German admiral ends with the empire's capital under Allied guns, and with a population that was told, for four years, that it was winning.The front · 30 October 1918Expand the mapSarikamisthe Suez CanalKutRomaniConstantinopleDamascusBeershebaBaghdadGazaAleppoNablusNazarethMudros-8MANPOWER ▾-10MUNITIONS ▾-10IMPERIAL CONTROL ▾Settled recordThe German ships, August 1914: kept out of the Straits. Entering the war, 1914: the fleet kept in the Bosphorus. Sarikamis, December 1914: the offensive postponed for a month for clothing, and then decided on the new facts. The Suez Canal, February 1915: the Fourth Army kept in Palestine. Gallipoli, April 1915: the reserve kept inland, and the landings contained. Kut, winter of 1915-16: the town stormed. Erzurum, 1916: the army fought the Russians outside the fortress. The Hejaz, 1916: evacuated. Sinai, 1916: the force kept by its wells. Baghdad, 1917: the line of the Diyala. Gaza, 1917: the line held and lengthened to Beersheba. Aqaba, 1917: the port lost to the Arab
